newsitem.title: INDIA: No clear signs of India industrial recovery - CMIE.
newsitem.headline: No clear signs of India industrial recovery - CMIE.

text.p: There are no clear indications that the Indian economy has reversed its recent slow down, an independent Bombay-based research firm said on Monday.
"The economy, in the meanwhile, has continued to splutter in finding its way out of the recent slowdown," the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said in a report.
"The most recent set of numbers neither deny the recovery in the growth in industrial production nor do they convincingly affirm," CMIE said in its February review of the Indian economy.

It said industrial production grew by 6.1 percent in the first quarter of financial 1996/97 (April-March) and 2.7 percent in the second quarter. The third quarter ended with an estimated growth of 3.4 percent, it said.

"The preliminary data available for January (1997) do point to a rapid and robust growth building up in the last quarter although a clearer picture would emerge only after more data becomes available," the report said.
Indian industry grew by 11.7 percent in 1995/96, according to the government's annual Economic Survey. It has projected growth of around 10 percent for 1996/97.
